name: Directional div layer overscan

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Directional div layer overscan

Mechanism: paint a div layer 2 viewports ahead of the scroll direction and 0.5 behind it (was 2 each side) so the layer scene and its repaint cost shrink by 30% with the same repaint cadence. Allowed: fast/layers/paint.rs painted_region. Forbidden: list layers, tile cache.
measurementPlanMarkdown: bm.sh e03 scroll-div-cards, scroll-uniform-list, 3 reps. Pass: heap peak down at least 10% on scroll-div-cards with CPU not worse, and `cargo test fast::tests::layer` green.
reportMarkdown:
## Directional div layer overscan Finished

Passed: false. Heap -6% and footprint -1.5% are below the -10% bar, CPU did not move, and two layer tests (`exposing_past_the_margin_repaints`, `a_repaint_at_a_shifted_offset_dirties_only_the_edge_tiles`) encode the symmetric region and the tile reuse across a re-centred repaint, so the asymmetric region dirties every tile. The footprint is mostly GPU tile textures (about 26 MB of 'graphics' for the visible tiles) and a third drawable, not the retained scene. Reverted.

Attempt Count: 1. Out-of-scope changes: none.
decisionMarkdown:
### Decision

Reverted failure. Finding: footprint of the scroll scenarios = visible tile textures (+26 MB), one more drawable at 120 fps (+16 MB IOSurface) and heap (+17 MB), see `footprint <pid>`.
